These are NOT logically equivalent for general simple graphs. Counterexample: let G have V={1,2,3} and E={{1,2}}, H have the same V and E={{1,2},{2,3}}, and f be the identity bijection. Every G edge maps to an H edge, yet inverse reflection fails for {2,3}, so G and H are NOT isomorphic. obs.wave2.quot118.ordinary-generating-fu.context: Analytic ordinary generating function of a real sequence on real convergence domain / power-series-convergence-domain
obs.wave2.quot118.ordinary-generating-fu.editorial_note: ProofWiki specifically defines generating function of a real sequence as sum of coefficient times nonnegative integer powers, and defines the resulting function only on z where the power series CONVERGES. The current approved context restricts the variable to real z, a mathematical specialization of the source's undifferentiated z; 0 always lies in D for an ordinary n≥0 power series. Do not silently equate this convergent analytic function with a formal power series in R[[z]], which exists independently of convergence and may have a different target object. Nor is this an exponential generating function involving 1/n!, a moment-generating function, or the double-index generating function the page separately describes. The coefficient extraction notation [z^n]G=a_n is a consequence of the power series presentation, not an extra inequivalent definition; uniqueness of analytic coefficients requires the appropriate analytic interpretation. Source sections: Definition for real sequence and convergence domain, Parameter, Extraction of Coefficient, Doubly Subscripted Sequence not promoted
obs.wave2.quot118.ordinary-generating-fu.text: For a real sequence (a_n)_{n≥0}, let D={z∈ℝ:∑_{n=0}^∞a_nz^n converges}. Its ordinary generating function is G_A:D→ℝ, defined by G_A(z)=∑_{n=0}^∞a_nz^n.
